requested_parts: Damage versus Destroy, Remove and Replace effects on Fear and survival
whether separate normal Powers’ Damage accumulates
whether normal Damage harms Dahan
whether Replace preserves Damage
answers.answer: Normal Power Damage marks Invaders and can accumulate with Damage from separate Powers and counterattacks within a turn; it normally does not harm Dahan or land. Destroy returns a piece regardless of Health and earns 1 Fear for a Town or 2 for a City. Remove returns pieces without destruction Fear. Replace removes one piece and adds another, retaining marked Damage; the replacement itself earns no Fear, but it is destroyed with normal Fear if retained Damage reaches its Health.

evidence.text: “Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. [FAQ if-an-invader-with-health-bonus-and-damage-is-moved-where-is-it-destroyed]

**Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

requested_parts: whether initially empty matching land becomes eligible during same Ravage card
whether newly arrived Invaders join a land already due to Ravage
answers.answer: Eligibility is determined for the card before its actions; changes during the card do not add newly eligible lands. Thus the initially empty matching land does not Ravage from that card. In a land already due to Ravage, newly arrived Invaders participate when its Ravage resolves.

evidence.text: Before resolving the actions from a card, determine which lands qualify; players choose the order of those lands. Changes during the card do not add newly eligible lands to that list. Determine eligibility anew for each later card, so a land newly occupied during an earlier Ravage card can Ravage under a later matching Ravage card. In a land already due to Ravage, newly arrived Invaders participate when its Ravage resolves. Resolve each land fully, including cascades and triggered effects, and check outcomes before proceeding to the next. answers.answer: If no legal Drowning result leaves humans placed legally, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands during that action; remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land afterward. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal, or destruction and triggers nothing; if no legal land exists, return humans to supply. Cleanup occurs before the outcome check.

At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. evidence.text: - **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. evidence.text: - **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. fact_assessments.observed: Prose gives nearest legal land and attached quotation places cleanup after the action; neither supplies judgment/physical distance when nearest is unclear.
fact_assessments.summary_support: Drowning supports post-action cleanup to nearest legal land, but the full frozen summary does not supply the mapped judgment/physical-distance method for an unclear nearest land.

fact_assessments.expected: Cleanup is not movement, Destroy, Remove or an action.
fact_assessments.observed: Despite the ordinary-language verb “Move” in its opening sentence, prose immediately and expressly says cleanup is not a move, action, removal or destruction; clause check agrees.
fact_assessments.summary_support: Drowning expressly says cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction.

fact_assessments.expected: If no legal land exists, return it to supply as cleanup.
fact_assessments.observed: Prose and quotation explicitly return humans to supply as cleanup when no legal land exists.
fact_assessments.summary_support: Drowning expressly returns humans to supply as cleanup if no legal land exists.

complete_original_proposal.reason: Nearest-legal-land cleanup, its classification and the no-legal-land result are correct. The mapped conditional method of using judgment/physical distance when nearest is unclear is absent from both the complete entry and the full summary. Provisional partial follows that mapped requirement; fresh adjudication is needed on whether this is a genuinely asked procedural detail or explanatory key background.
missing_requested_material_facts: Q81.request fact 1: when nearest legal land is unclear, use judgment/physical distance; this requirement is provisional pending the noted map-scope adjudication.

fact_assessments.expected: An illegally placed Invader cannot remain in Ocean between action trees.
fact_assessments.observed: Explicitly says humans cannot remain in Ocean between action trees.

excerpts.text: Humans cannot stay there between action trees:

fact_assessments.expected: Clean the illegally placed Invader up to the nearest legal land.
fact_assessments.observed: The attached quotation correctly says nearest-legal-land cleanup, but the answer directs “Push it to a non-Ocean land within the action if possible” and its coverage ruling for placement after the action tree says “Push to a non-Ocean legal land.” This applies the earlier failed-Drowning branch after the stipulated tree has finished.

excerpts.text: Remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land afterward.

fact_assessments.expected: That relocation is not movement and triggers no movement effects.
fact_assessments.observed: The answer and coverage ruling identify the case relocation as an actual in-action Push that may trigger movement effects. Although they also say later cleanup is not movement, this contradicts the requested post-tree relocation, which is itself cleanup.

excerpts.text: Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check.

complete_original_proposal.reason: Materially misapplies the failed-Drowning Push to the stipulated post-action-tree cleanup case. The complete quotation supplies the right cleanup rule, but the case-specific prose and coverage rulings contradict it.

contradictions.claim: Push it to a non-Ocean land within the action if possible; this is an actual Push and may trigger movement effects.
contradictions.why_material: The question expressly places the illegally remaining Invader after the primary action and every triggered action finish. Its relocation is then nearest-legal-land cleanup, not a new Push and not capable of triggering movement effects. Correct cleanup wording in the quotation and later sentence does not remove the contradictory case ruling.
